title: Airport Rides with Children: Confirming the Car Seat Plan
description: What to confirm before a family airport ride: the right child seat, who supplies it, vehicle fit, installation time and the return-trip arrangement.
cta: Plan your family airport ride with the details confirmed.
image_alt: A small linen rabbit resting on a folded charcoal cardigan on a wooden bench in soft afternoon light.
body:
Before booking an airport ride with children, confirm the restraint each child needs, who will supply it and whether the assigned vehicle can accommodate the full seating arrangement. A note saying “traveling with kids” is not a complete car-seat request. Obtain written confirmation for both the arrival and return journeys.

This checklist helps you organize that conversation. Seat availability, installation arrangements and any charges must be confirmed with your transportation provider for the specific reservation.

Start with each child, not just the vehicle size

NHTSA's car-seat guidance recommends choosing a restraint for the child's age and size, checking the manufacturer's height and weight limits, and ensuring it fits the vehicle. Follow the instructions for the particular seat and the vehicle owner's manual; a general age label is not enough to decide suitability.

Prepare a short list with each child's age, height and weight, plus the restraint type they currently use. Keep the units clear. If you are bringing your own seat, include its make and model and the intended rear-facing, forward-facing or booster configuration. You do not need to send a child's full name, birth certificate or travel-document photo to explain the equipment requirement.

Decide who supplies the seat

  • Bringing your own: tell the provider before booking and ask whether the vehicle can accommodate that model in its required configuration. Keep its instructions accessible offline and clarify who will install it.
  • Requesting a seat: ask what type and model can be supplied for your ride, whether it suits the information you provided, and whether the request is confirmed or still pending. Confirm any charge and installation arrangement.
  • Traveling with more than one child: list every restraint separately. Ask the provider to check the combined seating plan, including the adults, rather than treating each seat request in isolation.

Do not treat a child-seat checkbox or a free-text booking note as confirmation of a specific arrangement. Keep the provider's acknowledgment with the ride confirmation. If a requested seat cannot be confirmed, resolve an alternative before relying on that ride.

Ask about the whole seating and luggage layout

A vehicle's advertised passenger count does not answer whether your particular combination of restraints, adults and bags will work. NHTSA notes that not every car seat fits every vehicle. Ask for a configuration check instead of assuming that choosing a larger vehicle settles it.

Include strollers, checked bags and any seat being carried as luggage. For example, two adults, one rear-facing seat, one booster, a folded stroller and several bags form one combined request. This is an illustration of the details to provide, not a claim that a particular Koast vehicle fits them. The airport luggage planning checklist can help you describe the bags and folded equipment.

Leave room in the pickup plan for installation

Agree in advance who is responsible for installing each restraint and how the installation will be checked before departure. Ask how that time fits into the pickup and waiting arrangements. For an airport departure, plan backwards from your required terminal arrival so installation is not left to the final minute.

If you need help learning to use your seat, NHTSA's inspection-station resource can help you find a certified child passenger safety technician before travel. A booking confirmation is not a substitute for following the seat and vehicle instructions. If the supplied equipment differs from what was confirmed or cannot be used correctly, contact the provider and resolve it before the ride begins.

Confirm the return ride separately

If you bring a seat on the outbound ride, decide where it will be during the trip and how it will reach the return pickup. Do not assume the chauffeur or provider will store it while you travel. If a provider supplies the seat, confirm that the return reservation also includes the correct arrangement; it may involve a different vehicle.

When a vehicle, flight or pickup date changes, ask the provider to reconfirm the child-seat plan as part of the amendment. The flight-change checklist covers the other reservation details to update.

A request you can copy

Family airport ride: seating confirmation
Journey: [pickup and destination, local date and time; flight if relevant].
Travelers: [number of adults and children].
For each child: [age, height and weight with units; required restraint configuration].
Seat supply: [bringing our own make/model / requesting a suitable seat].
Other items: [bags, folded stroller dimensions and any additional equipment].
Please confirm the seat arrangement, vehicle compatibility, who installs it, time allowed, any charges and the separate return-trip plan.

For a Koast journey, review airport transfer options and contact reserve@koastride.com with the seating details before finalizing the arrangement. Keep the confirmed plan available to the adult traveling with the children.
